entries.disposition: Falsy sha256 uses the same pre-publication invalid-digest rejection as the malformed snapshot and artifact digest cases owned by coverage audit rejects incomplete, drifting and ambiguously referenced artifacts; it has no distinct effects or error stage.

Every assertIdentity caller supplies identityOnly output, or published added/removed already proven byte-for-byte equal to owner-generated identities, so an identity with unexpected fields cannot reach this defensive exact-fields guard.

Falsy source sha256 uses the same pre-publication invalid-source-metadata rejection as the malformed source digest case owned by coverage audit rejects incomplete, drifting and ambiguously referenced artifacts; it has no distinct effects or error stage.

Canonical zero-counter path ordering is exercised with zero-bearing source files in both forward and reverse raw-report order by coverage audit occurrences identify raw sibling counters before zero filtering.

Canonical normalized previous-review ordering for unique paths is exercised in both directions, while duplicate source paths are rejected by the existing malformed snapshot/review owner; comparator equality compatibility has no separate public outcome.
